purpose: Model-based meaning-preservation reads for (source, rewrite) pairs, the pair that style-transfer work reports beside every style score. Channel mis is the Mutual Implication Score (Babakov et al. 2022), a symmetric 0-1 RoBERTa-large read of whether each text implies the other, loaded at run time from s-nlp/Mutual_Implication_Score through the mutual-implication-score package; those weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, are never vendored, and the license is carried in the output. Channel sbert is the cosine of sentence-transformers embeddings through the shared SETEC embedding backend (default mxbai). Reports per-pair values and per-channel mean, median, minimum and quartiles; a channel whose model cannot load is dropped with a warning and the run abstains only when none loads. Both models truncate at 512 tokens, so long pairs are warned about. No cut-off is calibrated.
use_when: You rewrote passages (style transfer, register shift, a reviser run) and want a model read of how much meaning each rewrite kept
You need a content-fidelity number to report beside a style or register score
do_not_use_when: You need to catch dropped facts, negation flips or entity swaps (use semantic_preservation_check)
You want a quality judgment or a pass/fail gate
Your pairs are much longer than a paragraph and you cannot chunk them (both models truncate)

artifacts: results.meaning_preservation.per_pair: mis, sbert_cosine, word counts, length_ratio

compute.cost_note: One RoBERTa-large pair pass (MIS) and two embedding passes (SBERT) per pair; GPU helps for large sets, CPU is fine for a few hundred paragraphs.

examples.description: Both channels for a set of rewrite pairs
SBERT channel only, with a small embedding model

references: Large Scale Evaluation of Mutual Implication Score (Babakov et al. 2022, ACL Findings): https://aclanthology.org/2022.findings-acl.153/
